passage: I'm Gopika, and I sit two rows behind Madhav in Class 10. On Tuesday, Mr Kurian read out his test mark and said, "Maybe try opening a book this year." A few people laughed. I saw Madhav's neck go red, his jaw working, his fingers digging into the desk edge. He stood up so fast his chair scraped. I honestly thought he would shout something he couldn't take back. Instead he said, in a tight voice, "May I go to the washroom, sir?" and walked out. Through the window I saw him at the tap, splashing cold water on his face again and again. When he came back, his shoulders were down. After class he went up to Mr Kurian and said calmly, "That comment hurt. Can we talk about my marks another time?" I don't know what was going on in his head, but I know what he didn't say.

qa.q: What did Madhav do at the tap?
qa.a: Madhav was splashing cold water on his face again and again.

qa.q: What might Madhav's red neck and digging fingers suggest about how he felt?
qa.a: They suggest Madhav was flooded with anger and humiliation after the comment, though Gopika could not know for sure.

qa.q: Which choice did Madhav make, and why was it wise?
qa.a: Madhav left for the washroom and cooled down with water before speaking, so he could raise the hurt calmly instead of saying something he couldn't take back.

qa.q: How might Mr Kurian have felt when Madhav said calmly that the comment hurt?
qa.a: Mr Kurian may have felt caught off guard and perhaps sorry, since a calm complaint is harder to dismiss than an outburst.

grounding: A teenager provoked by a teacher is visibly flooded with anger, steps out and uses cold water so the surge falls before speaking.

passage:
Monday. When his younger sister Madhuri read his message to a friend out loud at dinner, Tenzin's face burned and his pulse thudded in his ears. "You're a pathetic little snoop and nobody likes you!" he yelled. Madhuri's face crumpled. He lay awake that night wishing he could take it back.
Thursday. She grabbed his phone again, laughing. The same heat rushed up his neck; the room seemed to shrink to her grinning face. Tenzin put the phone down, said, "I'm going for a run," and pounded around the colony twice until his breath came back.
Saturday. Tenzin knocked on her door. "What I said on Monday was cruel. I'm sorry. But reading my stuff isn't okay." Madhuri nodded, eyes down. "I know. Sorry."

qa.q: What did Tenzin do on Thursday when the heat rushed up his neck?
qa.a: Tenzin said he was going for a run and pounded around the colony twice.

qa.q: What was Tenzin feeling the night after Monday's dinner?
qa.a: Tenzin felt regret and guilt, lying awake wishing he could take back what he yelled.

qa.q: What changed between Monday and Thursday, and why did it help?
qa.a: On Thursday Tenzin noticed the rising heat and left for a run before speaking, so the anger dropped and he could apologise and set a limit calmly on Saturday.

qa.q: How might Madhuri have felt when Tenzin yelled on Monday?
qa.a: Madhuri was hurt; her face crumpled when she was called a pathetic snoop.

grounding: A teenager's heat, pounding pulse and narrowed focus lead to cruel words, and next time he steps away for a run before speaking.
